question: If the speed of a boat moving against the current is 18 km/hr, what is the speed of the stream if the boat's speed downstream is 50% greater than its speed upstream ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed = 18 + 50% of 18 = 27 kmph

Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Speed of stream = (27 − 18) ÷ 2 = 4.5 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat upstream (U) = 18 kmph

Speed of boat downstream (D) is 50% greater than upstream speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f87106cfe1e1cb613dfb1b2149fd542b56b762ab7be407b7e3aeca632931fc4.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed (D) = U + (U × Percentage Increase)

Speed of Stream (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ D = 18 + (18 × 50 ÷ 100)

⇒ D = 18 + 9 = 27 kmph

⇒ v = (27 − 18) ÷ 2

⇒ v = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

The speed of a boat in still water is the average of its downstream and upstream speeds: u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Downstream vs Upstream

Downstream speed occurs when the boat moves in the direction of the stream (u + v). Upstream speed occurs when the boat moves against the stream (u − v).

Relative Speed Ratio

The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream can be directly found using (D + U) : (D − U).
